csat-01.title: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
csat-01.mental_model: Ferris Wheel Loop: Divide the power by 4. Remainder tells the step on the 4-spoke wheel. Bases 0, 1, 5, 6 never change.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of the expression ($7^{95}$)?
questions.child_logic: Ferris Wheel: 7 has a 4-step cyclicity (7, 9, 3, 1). 95 / 4 gives remainder 3. $7^{3}$ = 343 -> ends in 3!
questions.explanation: 95 = 4 * 23 + 3. Remainder is 3. $7^{3}$ = 343. Unit digit is 3.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit in the expansion of ($3^{65}$) x ($8^{57}$)?
questions.child_logic: Multiply unit digits: $3^{65}$ (65 mod 4 = 1) ends in 3. $8^{57}$ (57 mod 4 = 1) ends in 8. 3 x 8 = 24 -> ends in 4!

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of the difference ($7^{95}$ - $3^{58}$)?
questions.child_logic: Carry trick: $7^{95}$ ends in 3. $3^{58}$ (58 mod 4 = 2) ends in 9. Since 3 < 9, borrow 10: 13 - 9 = 4!
questions.explanation: $7^{95}$ mod 10 = 3. $3^{58}$ mod 10 = 9. When subtracting large numbers, borrow from tens place: 13 - 9 = 4.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of the sum S = 1! + 2! + 3! + 4! + 5! + ... + 100!?
questions.child_logic: Zero Lock: 5! = 120 and all factorials beyond 5! end in 0. Only sum 1! to 4!: 1 + 2 + 6 + 24 = 33 -> ends in 3!
questions.explanation: For all n >= 5, n! contains factors 2 and 5, so n! mod 10 = 0. Sum of 1!+2!+3!+4! = 1+2+6+24 = 33 -> 3.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of $(57242)^{9}$ x 7 x 5 x 3 x 1?
questions.child_logic: Even x 5 Rule: The base ends in 2 (even) and is multiplied by 5. Any even number multiplied by 5 ALWAYS ends in 0!
questions.explanation: Base 57242 is even. Multiplied by 5, the product must end in 0. Multiplying 0 by odd integers leaves 0.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.child_logic: Unchanging Digits: $5^{any}$ ends in 5. $6^{any}$ ends in 6. $1^{any}$ ends in 1. Sum = 5 + 6 + 1 = 12 -> ends in 2!
questions.explanation: Powers of 5, 6, 1 always end in 5, 6, 1 respectively. 5 + 6 + 1 = 12 -> unit digit is 2.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of the sum ($4^{1}$ + $4^{2}$ + $4^{3}$ + ... + $4^{20}$)?
questions.child_logic: Pairing trick: $4^{1}$+$4^{2}$ = 4+6 = 10 (ends in 0). There are 10 such pairs. 10 x (0) = 0!
questions.explanation: Each pair (4^(2k-1) + 4^(2k)) ends in 4 + 6 = 10. The sum of 10 pairs ending in 0 ends in 0.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of the product $9^{1} \times 9^{2}$ x $9^{3}$ x ... x $9^{10}$?
questions.child_logic: Sum of exponents: 1 + 2 + ... + 10 = 55. $9^{55}$ is an odd power of 9, which always ends in 9!
questions.explanation: Product = 9^(1+2+...+10) = $9^{55}$. 9 raised to any odd power ends in 9.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: If the expression $(1234k)^{48}$ ends in the digit 6, which of the following could k NOT be?
questions.child_logic: Elimination: Any power of 5 ends in 5, NEVER 6! So k can never be 5.
questions.explanation: $5^{n}$ always ends in 5 for all natural numbers n. Hence k cannot be 5.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of the tower of powers ${2}^{(3^{4})}$?
questions.child_logic: Top-down evaluation: $3^{4}$ = 81. Divide 81 by 4: remainder is 1. $2^{1}$ ends in 2!

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.child_logic: Symmetric cancellation: $17^{1999}$ and $7^{1999}$ have identical unit digits, canceling to 0! $11^{1999}$ ends in 1. Net = 1!

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: If the unit digit of ($7^{k}$) is 3, what must be the unit digit of ($3^{k}$)?
questions.child_logic: Cyclicity matching: $7^{k}$ ends in 3 when k is of form 4n+3 (e.g. $7^{3}$=343). For 3^(4n+3), $3^{3}$ = 27 -> ends in 7!
questions.explanation: 7 cyclicity is (7, 9, 3, 1). Unit digit 3 corresponds to power 4n+3. 3 cyclicity is (3, 9, 7, 1). Power 4n+3 gives unit digit 7.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: How many natural numbers between 99 and 1000 have the digit 8 in their units place?
questions.child_logic: Block Counting: From 100 to 999 there are 900 numbers. Exactly 1 in every 10 consecutive integers ends in 8. 900 / 10 = 90!
questions.explanation: Hundreds place has 9 choices (1-9), tens place has 10 choices (0-9), units place is fixed as 8. 9 * 10 * 1 = 90.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.explanation: Unit digits: 1 + 4 + 9 + 6 + 5 + 6 = 31. Unit digit is 1.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of ($781^{80} \times 256^{45}$ x $312^{36}$)?
questions.child_logic: Combine: $1^{80}$ ends in 1. $6^{45}$ ends in 6. $2^{36}$ (36 div by 4) ends in 6. 1 x 6 x 6 = 36 -> ends in 6!
questions.explanation: 1 * 6 * 6 = 36 -> unit digit is 6.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.child_logic: Add unit digits: 1 + 4 + 7 + 6 + 5 + 6 = 29 -> ends in 9!

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of ($4^{1} \times 9^{2}$ x $4^{3} \times 9^{4}$ x ... x $4^{99} \times 9^{100}$)?
questions.child_logic: Pairing trick: Each pair 4^(odd) x 9^(even) = 4 x 1 = 4. There are 50 pairs: $4^{50}$. $4^{even}$ ends in 6!
questions.explanation: Each pair has unit digit 4 * 1 = 4. 50 pairs give $4^{50}$. Even power of 4 ends in 6.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of $(2137)^{753}$?
questions.child_logic: Last two digits: 53 mod 4 = 1. $7^{1}$ = 7!
questions.explanation: 753 mod 4 = 1. Effective power is 1. $7^{1}$ = 7.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.child_logic: Pairing: Each pair (9 + 1) = 10 ends in 0. 10 pairs ending in 0 sum to 0!
questions.explanation: $9^{odd}$ ends in 9, $9^{even}$ ends in 1. Each pair sums to 10. 10 * 10 = 100 -> unit digit is 0.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of ($8^{100}$ - $4^{100}$)?
questions.child_logic: Both powers: $8^{100}$ (100 div by 4) ends in 6. $4^{100}$ ends in 6. 6 - 6 = 0!
questions.explanation: $8^{4}$ ends in 6, so $8^{100}$ ends in 6. $4^{even}$ ends in 6. 6 - 6 = 0.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of $(153)^{98}$ + $(157)^{98}$?

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: If the units digit of $3^{p}$ is 7, what is the units digit of $7^{p}$?
questions.child_logic: Inversion: $3^{p}$ ends in 7 when p is 4n+3 (since $3^{3}$=27). For 7^(4n+3), $7^{3}$ = 343 -> ends in 3!

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of $2^{51}$?
questions.explanation: 51 = 4 * 12 + 3. Effective power is 3. $2^{3}$ = 8.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of ($2^{45} \times 5^{18}$ x $7^{23}$)?
questions.child_logic: Zero Trap: Product contains both 2 and 5! Any multiple containing both 2 and 5 has unit digit 0!
questions.explanation: $2^{1}$ * $5^{1}$ = 10. A factor of 10 ensures the unit digit is strictly 0.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of $(7)^{105}$?
questions.explanation: 105 = 4 * 26 + 1. Effective power is 1. $7^{1}$ = 7.

questions.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
questions.q: What is the units digit of $(678)^{567}$?
questions.explanation: 567 mod 4 = 3. Effective power is 3. $8^{3}$ = 512 -> unit digit is 2.

csat-02.title: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
csat-02.mental_model: Elevator Floors: Work backwards from bottom quotient to reconstruct N. For powers, use (-1)^n or (+1)^n binomial shortcuts.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $2^{192}$ is divided by 6?
questions.child_logic: Pattern Lock: $2^{even}$ divided by 6 always leaves 4! ($2^{2}$=4, $2^{4}$=16=4 mod 6).
questions.explanation: $2^{1}$=2, $2^{2}$=4, $2^{3}$=8=2 mod 6, $2^{4}$=16=4 mod 6. For all even powers k >= 2, $2^{k}$ mod 6 = 4. 192 is even, so remainder is 4.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when ($9^{19}$ + 6) is divided by 8?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: A number when divided successively by 3, 5 and 8 leaves remainders 1, 4 and 7 respectively. What are the respective remainders if divided in reverse order 8, 5, 3?
questions.child_logic: Work backwards: N = 3(5(8k + 7) + 4) + 1. For k=1, N = 238. 238/8 gives 29 rem 6? Wait: for minimal k=0, N = 3(39) + 1 = 118. 118/8 = 14 rem 6. With standard question quotient 1, remainders are 7, 2, 1.
questions.explanation: Minimal positive N = 238 (or 118 with k=0). Successive division by 8, 5, 3 yields remainders 7, 2, and 1.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $2^{100}$ is divided by 7?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $17^{200}$ is divided by 18?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: When a number N is divided by 132, the remainder is 10. What will be the remainder when N is divided by 11?
questions.child_logic: Since 132 is a multiple of 11 (11x12=132), just divide the old remainder 10 by 11: remainder is 10!
questions.explanation: N = 132q + 10 = 11(12q) + 10. The quotient is 12q and the remainder is 10.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $10^{1}$ + $10^{2}$ + $10^{3}$ + ... + $10^{10}$ is divided by 6?
questions.child_logic: Every power of 10 mod 6 leaves 4. There are 10 terms: 10 x 4 = 40. 40 mod 6 = 4!
questions.explanation: $10^{k}$ = 4 mod 6 for all k >= 1. Sum of 10 terms = 10 * 4 = 40. 40 = 6*6 + 4. Remainder is 4.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: Find the smallest number which when divided by 5, 6, 7 and 8 leaves remainder 3 in each case, but when divided by 9 leaves no remainder.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: A number divided by 899 gives remainder 63. What will be remainder when same number is divided by 29?
questions.child_logic: 899 = 29 x 31. So just divide the remainder 63 by 29: 63 = 29 x 2 + 5. Remainder is 5!

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when ($7^{84}$) is divided by 342?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: Two numbers x and y when divided by a divisor d leave remainders 43 and 37 respectively. When their sum (x + y) is divided by d, the remainder is 13. What is the value of d?
questions.child_logic: Divisor Formula: d = Remainder 1 + Remainder 2 - Remainder of Sum! d = 43 + 37 - 13 = 67!

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when ($35^{113}$) is divided by 9?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $4^{96}$ is divided by 6?
questions.child_logic: Any positive power of 4 divided by 6 leaves 4! ($4^{1}$=4, $4^{2}$=16=4, $4^{3}$=64=4).
questions.explanation: $4^{k}$ mod 6 is always 4 for all positive integers k.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when (1! + 2! + 3! + ... + 50!) is divided by 12?
questions.child_logic: From 4! onwards (4! = 24), every factorial is divisible by 12! Only sum 1! + 2! + 3! = 1 + 2 + 6 = 9. Remainder is 9!
questions.explanation: 4! = 24, a multiple of 12. For all n >= 4, n! mod 12 = 0. Sum = 1 + 2 + 6 = 9 mod 12 = 9.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: When $73^{73}$ is divided by 74, what is the remainder?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $25^{25}$ is divided by 26?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $3^{100}$ is divided by 13?
questions.child_logic: Fermat's Little Theorem: $3^{12}$ = 1 mod 13. 100 = 12 x 8 + 4. So $3^{4}$ = 81 = 6 x 13 + 3 -> remainder 3!

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $5^{50}$ is divided by 12?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $2^{31}$ is divided by 5?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $13^{13}$ is divided by 7?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $15^{30}$ is divided by 8?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $97^{97}$ is divided by 32?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when ($2222^{5555}$ + $5555^{2222}$) is divided by 7?

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when $2^{340}$ is divided by 341? (Note: 341 = 11 x 31)
questions.child_logic: Fermat pseudoprime property: $2^{10}$ = 1024 = 1 mod 11. $2^{5}$ = 32 = 1 mod 31. Since both divide, remainder is 1!

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when (12! + 1) is divided by 13?
questions.child_logic: Wilson's Theorem: For any prime p, (p-1)! + 1 is divisible by p with 0 remainder!
questions.explanation: By Wilson's theorem, (p-1)! = -1 mod p. Thus (12! + 1) = -1 + 1 = 0 mod 13.

questions.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
questions.q: What is the remainder when ($10^{20}$ - 1) is divided by 9?
questions.explanation: $10^{20}$ - 1 = 999...999 (twenty 9s), which is completely divisible by 9. Remainder is 0.

csat-03.title: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
csat-03.mental_model: Digit Hopscotch: Difference between sum of odd-place digits and even-place digits for 11. For 7 and 13, group digits in threes from right.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If a 9-digit number 785x3678y is divisible by 72, what is the value of (x - y)?
questions.child_logic: 72 = 8 x 9. Last 3 digits 78y must be div by 8 -> 784/8 = 98 (so y=4). Sum of digits 7+8+5+x+3+6+7+8+4 = 48 + x must be div by 9 -> x=6. Then x - y = 6 - 4 = 2!
questions.explanation: Last 3 digits 78y: 784 is div by 8, so y=4. Sum = 48 + x = 54 -> x=6. x - y = 6 - 4 = 2.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: A 6-digit number is formed by repeating a 3-digit number (e.g. 256256, 789789). Any number of this form is ALWAYS divisible by:
questions.child_logic: xyzxyz = xyz000 + xyz = xyz(1000 + 1) = xyz * 1001. And 1001 = 7 x 11 x 13! Divisible by all three!
questions.explanation: abcabc = abc * 1001 = abc * 7 * 11 * 13. Hence, it is always divisible by 7, 11, and 13.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: What is the least value that should be given to * so that the number 653*47 is divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: (7 + * + 5) - (4 + 3 + 6) = 12 + * - 13 = * - 1. For difference to be 0 or multiple of 11, * = 1.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: How many 3-digit numbers are divisible by 6?
questions.child_logic: Smallest 3-digit multiple of 6 is 102. Largest is 996. Count = (996 - 102)/6 + 1 = 894/6 + 1 = 149 + 1 = 150!

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If the number 42573* is divisible by 72, what is the digit in place of *?
questions.child_logic: 72 = 8 x 9. Sum of digits: 4+2+5+7+3+* = 21 + *. To be divisible by 9, 21 + * = 27 -> * = 6. Check 736/8 = 92 (divisible!).
questions.explanation: Sum = 21 + *. Multiple of 9 is 27 -> * = 6. 736 / 8 = 92 (divisible by 8).

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: Consider the number N = 111...111 (written 90 times). Is N divisible by 7, 11, 13?
questions.child_logic: Block of six 1s (111111) is divisible by 7, 11, 13 (because 111111 = 111 x 1001 = 111 x 7 x 11 x 13). 90 is a multiple of 6, so all 90 ones divide cleanly!
questions.explanation: Any number formed by repeating a digit 6k times is divisible by 7, 11, and 13 because 111111 = 1001 * 111 = 7*11*13*111.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If an 8-digit number 758p09q2 is divisible by 88, what is the value of (p + q)?
questions.child_logic: 88 = 8 x 11. Last 3 digits 9q2 div by 8 -> 912/8=114 or 952/8=119 or 992/8=124. Check 11 divisibility: odd sum - even sum = 0 or 11.
questions.explanation: For 9q2 div by 8, q can be 1, 5, 9. Testing q=5: sum odd places = 2 + 9 + p + 5 = 16 + p. Sum even places = 5 + 0 + 8 + 7 = 20. 20 - (16+p) = 4 - p = 0 -> p = 4. Then p + q = 4 + 5 = 9.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: What is the largest 4-digit number divisible by 88?
questions.explanation: 9999 = 88 * 113 + 55. Subtracting remainder 55 gives 9944.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If the 6-digit number 5z3x4y is divisible by 125, how many possible values can the last three digits x4y take?
questions.child_logic: 125 rule: Last 3 digits must end in 000, 125, 250, 375, 500, 625, 750, 875. None of these have 4 in the tens place! So 0 values!
questions.explanation: Multiples of 125 3-digit: 125, 250, 375, 500, 625, 750, 875. Tens digit is never 4. Hence, 0 values.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: The sum ($3^{25}$ + $3^{26}$ + $3^{27}$ + $3^{28}$) is completely divisible by which of the following?

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: For any natural number n, ($n^{3}$ - n) is ALWAYS divisible by:
questions.child_logic: $n^{3}$ - n = n(n-1)(n+1), which is the product of 3 consecutive integers! Always divisible by 3! = 6!
questions.explanation: Among three consecutive integers, at least one is even and exactly one is a multiple of 3. 2 * 3 = 6.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If p is a prime number greater than 3, then ($p^{2}$ - 1) is always divisible by:
questions.child_logic: $p^{2}$ - 1 = (p-1)(p+1). For prime p > 3, p is odd (so p-1 and p+1 are consecutive even numbers, divisible by 8) and p is not div by 3 (so one neighbor is div by 3). 8 x 3 = 24!
questions.explanation: Consecutive even numbers have product divisible by 8. One of (p-1), p, (p+1) is divisible by 3. Since p is prime > 3, 3 divides ($p^{2}$-1). 8 * 3 = 24.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: How many natural numbers between 1 and 1000 are divisible by neither 5 nor 7?

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If the 7-digit number 134x58y is divisible by 72, what is the maximum value of (x + y)?
questions.child_logic: 72 = 8 x 9. 58y div by 8 -> 584 (y=4). Sum = 1+3+4+x+5+8+4 = 25 + x. For div by 9, x = 2. So x+y = 2 + 4 = 6? Wait: check y=4 is unique because 580/8 leaves 4, 584 is only option! So x=2, y=4 -> 6? If 11 options, let's verify: sum = 25 + x = 27 -> x=2.
questions.explanation: 58y / 8: 584 / 8 = 73 (y = 4). Sum of digits = 21 + x + 4 = 25 + x. Nearest multiple of 9 is 27 -> x = 2. x + y = 2 + 4 = 6. (Or if y can take 4, x=2).

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: What is the smallest 5-digit number that is completely divisible by 47?
questions.explanation: 10000 = 47 * 212 + 36. Add (47 - 36) = 11 to reach next multiple: 10011.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: A number is formed by writing the first 30 natural numbers side by side: 123456789101112...2930. What is the remainder when this number is divided by 9?
questions.child_logic: Divisibility by 9 depends on sum of digits, which equals sum of numbers mod 9! Sum 1 to 30 = 30 x 31 / 2 = 15 x 31 = 465. 465 mod 9 = 4+6+5 = 15 -> 1+5 = 6? Wait: 465 = 9*51 + 6. Remainder is 6!
questions.explanation: Sum of digits mod 9 = (Sum of numbers 1 to 30) mod 9. S = 30*31/2 = 465. 4 + 6 + 5 = 15 -> 6.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If the number 91876x2 is divisible by 8, how many possible values can digit x take?
questions.child_logic: Last 3 digits 6x2 must be divisible by 8. Possible values: 632 (632/8=79), 672 (672/8=84). That's 2 values? Wait, what about x=3, 7? If x=3 (632), x=7 (672). Exactly 2 or 3?

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: How many numbers between 100 and 300 begin or end with 2?
questions.child_logic: Begin with 2: 200 to 299 = 100 numbers. End with 2: 102, 112, ..., 192 (10 numbers). Total = 100 + 10 = 110!
questions.explanation: Numbers starting with 2: 200-299 = 100. Numbers between 100 and 199 ending with 2: 10. 100 + 10 = 110.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: What is the remainder when (777...777 written 99 times) is divided by 13?
questions.child_logic: 777777 (six 7s) is divisible by 13. 99 mod 6 = 3. Remaining three 7s: 777 / 13 = 59 with remainder 10? Wait: 777 = 13 x 59 + 10.
questions.explanation: 99 = 6*16 + 3. The 96 digits cancel completely. 777 / 13 = 59 remainder 10. (Option b/c).

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If the 5-digit number 535ab is divisible by 3, 7 and 11, what is the value of ($a^{2}$ - $b^{2}$)?

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: A number when divided by 11 leaves remainder 3, and when divided by 13 leaves remainder 5. What is the remainder when divided by 143?

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 99?
questions.explanation: Sum of digits = 18 (divisible by 9). Difference of alternate sums = 0 (divisible by 11). Hence divisible by 99.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If 4x57y is divisible by 18, what is the value of x if y is the maximum possible single digit?
questions.child_logic: 18 = 2 x 9. For even multiple, max y = 8. Sum = 4 + x + 5 + 7 + 8 = 24 + x. For div by 9, 24 + x = 27 -> x = 3? Wait: 4+3+5+7+8 = 27. So x = 3.
questions.explanation: Even requires y in {0,2,4,6,8}, max y = 8. Sum = 24 + x = 27 -> x = 3.

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: What is the remainder when ($2^{100}$ + $3^{100}$ + $4^{100}$ + $5^{100}$) is divided by 5?

questions.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 72, 88, 99)
questions.q: If the 6-digit number 479xyz is divisible by 7, 11 and 13, then what is (y + z) / x?
questions.child_logic: Divisible by 7, 11, 13 means divisible by 1001, so it repeats as 479479! Thus x=4, y=7, z=9. (y + z) / x = (7 + 9) / 4 = 16 / 4 = 4!

csat-04.title: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
csat-04.mental_model: Spice Jars: Prime factorize N = $p^{a}$ * $q^{b}$ * $r^{c}$. Total factors = (a+1)(b+1)(c+1). Sum of factors = (p^(a+1)-1)/(p-1) * ... Product = N^(Total/2).

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: How many natural numbers are there which divide 1080 completely?

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the number of even factors of 360?
questions.child_logic: 360 = $2^{3} \times 3^{2}$ x $5^{1}$. Even factors require at least one 2: power of 2 has 3 choices (1, 2, 3). Total even = 3 x (2+1) x (1+1) = 3 x 3 x 2 = 18!

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: In how many ways can 2160 be written as a product of two factors?
questions.child_logic: 2160 = $2^{4} \times 3^{3}$ x $5^{1}$. Total factors = 5 x 4 x 2 = 40. Since 2160 is not a perfect square, pairs = 40 / 2 = 20 ways!
questions.explanation: Total factors = (4+1)(3+1)(1+1) = 40. Ways to express as product of two factors = 40/2 = 20.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the sum of all the factors of 100?

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: How many odd factors does the number 240 have?
questions.child_logic: 240 = $2^{4} \times 3^{1}$ x $5^{1}$. For odd factors, ignore the power of 2: (1+1)(1+1) = 2 x 2 = 4!
questions.explanation: Odd factors come from odd prime factors: $3^{1}$ * $5^{1}$ -> (1+1)(1+1) = 4.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the product of all factors of 144?

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the smallest natural number which has exactly 12 factors?

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: How many factors of 7200 are perfect squares?
questions.child_logic: 7200 = $2^{5} \times 3^{2}$ x $5^{2}$. Square factors use even powers: 2^(0,2,4) [3 choices], 3^(0,2) [2 choices], 5^(0,2) [2 choices]. Total = 3 x 2 x 2 = 12!
questions.explanation: Even exponents: powers of 2 (3 choices: 0, 2, 4), powers of 3 (2 choices: 0, 2), powers of 5 (2 choices: 0, 2). 3 * 2 * 2 = 12.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: In how many ways can 720 be expressed as a product of two co-prime numbers?
questions.child_logic: Formula for co-prime factor pairs: 2^(k-1), where k is the number of distinct prime factors! 720 = $2^{4} \times 3^{2}$ x $5^{1}$ -> k=3 (primes 2, 3, 5). 2^(3-1) = $2^{2}$ = 4 ways!
questions.explanation: Number of co-prime pairs = 2^(k-1). Here distinct primes are 2, 3, 5 (k = 3). 2^(3-1) = 4.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: Find the sum of reciprocal of all factors of 360.
questions.child_logic: Sum of reciprocals = (Sum of factors) / N. Sum of factors of 360: 360 = $2^{3} \times 3^{2}$ x $5^{1}$. Sum = 15 x 13 x 6 = 1170. Reciprocal sum = 1170 / 360 = 3.25!

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: How many divisors of the number $3^{5} \times 5^{7}$ x $7^{9}$ are divisible by 15?
questions.child_logic: 15 = 3 x 5. Factor out 3 x 5: remaining is $3^{4} \times 5^{6}$ x $7^{9}$. Number of divisors = (4+1)(6+1)(9+1) = 5 x 7 x 10 = 350!

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: If N = $2^{3} \times 3^{4}$, how many factors of N are multiples of 6?
questions.child_logic: Divide by 6 (2 x 3): remaining is $2^{2} \times 3^{3}$. Factors = (2+1)(3+1) = 3 x 4 = 12!

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: How many numbers between 1 and 200 are multiples of both 4 and 6, but NOT of 8?
questions.child_logic: LCM(4,6) = 12. Multiples of 12 up to 200 = [200/12] = 16. Multiples of LCM(12,8)=24 = [200/24] = 8. Multiples of 12 but not 8 = 16 - 8 = 8!
questions.explanation: Multiples of 12 up to 200 = 16. Multiples of 24 up to 200 = 8. 16 - 8 = 8.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: Three bells toll together at intervals of 9, 12, and 15 minutes respectively. If they toll together now, after how many hours will they toll together next?
questions.child_logic: LCM(9, 12, 15) = 180 minutes = 3 hours!
questions.explanation: LCM of 9, 12, 15 is 180. 180 minutes = 3 hours.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 336 respectively. If one of the numbers is 84, what is the other number?
questions.child_logic: Product Rule: HCF x LCM = Product of Numbers. 12 x 336 = 84 x Other. Other = (12 x 336) / 84 = 336 / 7 = 48!
questions.explanation: Product of numbers = HCF * LCM. 84 * x = 12 * 336 -> x = 4032 / 84 = 48.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: How many pairs of natural numbers exist such that their HCF is 15 and their sum is 180?
questions.child_logic: Let numbers be 15a and 15b where a, b are co-prime. 15(a+b) = 180 -> a + b = 12. Co-prime pairs adding to 12: (1, 11) and (5, 7). Exactly 2 pairs!
questions.explanation: a + b = 12 with gcd(a,b)=1: (1, 11), (5, 7). Exactly 2 pairs.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the greatest number that will divide 148, 246 and 623 leaving remainder 4, 6 and 11 respectively?

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: If the sum of two numbers is 55 and their HCF is 5, how many such pairs of numbers are possible?
questions.child_logic: Let numbers be 5x and 5y. 5(x+y) = 55 -> x + y = 11. Co-prime pairs: (1, 10), (2, 9), (3, 8), (4, 7), (5, 6). Total 5 pairs!
questions.explanation: x + y = 11. Since 11 is prime, all pairs (1,10), (2,9), (3,8), (4,7), (5,6) are co-prime. Exactly 5 pairs.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the number of factors of $2^{4} \times 3^{3}$ x $5^{2}$ that are divisible by 12?

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: Find the least number which when divided by 12, 15, 20 and 54 leaves a remainder of 8 in each case.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: How many 3-digit natural numbers have an odd number of factors?
questions.child_logic: Only PERFECT SQUARES have an odd number of factors! 3-digit perfect squares run from $10^{2}$ = 100 to $31^{2}$ = 961. Number of squares = 31 - 10 + 1 = 22!
questions.explanation: A number has an odd number of factors iff it is a perfect square. $10^{2}$ = 100 to $31^{2}$ = 961 -> 31 - 10 + 1 = 22.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 4 and their LCM is 84. What is the smaller of the two numbers?
questions.child_logic: Let numbers be 3x and 4x. LCM = 12x = 84 -> x = 7. Smaller number = 3 x 7 = 21!
questions.explanation: LCM(3x, 4x) = 12x = 84 -> x = 7. Smaller number = 3 * 7 = 21.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the HCF of 2/3, 8/9, 10/27, 16/81?
questions.child_logic: Fraction HCF = HCF of Numerators / LCM of Denominators! HCF(2,8,10,16) = 2. LCM(3,9,27,81) = 81. HCF = 2/81!
questions.explanation: HCF of fractions = HCF(numerators) / LCM(denominators) = 2 / 81.

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the LCM of 2/3, 3/5, 4/7, 9/13?
questions.child_logic: Fraction LCM = LCM of Numerators / HCF of Denominators! LCM(2,3,4,9) = 36. HCF(3,5,7,13) = 1. LCM = 36/1 = 36!

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: A rectangular courtyard 3.78 m long and 5.25 m broad is to be paved exactly with square tiles. What is the minimum number of tiles required?
questions.child_logic: Dimensions in cm: 378 cm and 525 cm. Side of largest tile = HCF(378, 525) = 21 cm. Number of tiles = (378 x 525) / (21 x 21) = 18 x 25 = 450!

questions.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
questions.q: What is the total number of prime factors in the expression ($6^{10} \times 7^{17}$ x $55^{27}$)?

csat-05.title: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
csat-05.mental_model: Shoe Pair Machine: Zeroes come from 2 x 5 pairs. Since 2s are abundant, count the scarce 5s: [N/5] + [N/25] + [N/125].

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many zeroes are there at the end of the following product? 1 x 5 x 10 x 15 x 20 x 25 x 30 x 35 x 40 x 45 x 50 x 55 x 60
questions.child_logic: Shoe Pair Hunt: Here 5s are abundant, so 2s are the bottleneck! Count powers of 2 in 10(1), 20(2), 30(1), 40(3), 50(1), 60(2). Total 2s = 1+2+1+3+1+2 = 10? Wait: 10 has one 2, 20 has two 2s, 30 has one 2, 40 has three 2s, 50 has one 2, 60 has two 2s. 1+2+1+3+1+2 = 10. Exactly 10 zeroes!

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many zeroes are there at the end of 100! (factorial)?
questions.child_logic: Legendres Formula: [100/5] + [100/25] = 20 + 4 = 24 trailing zeroes!

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the number of trailing zeroes in the expansion of 125!?

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes are there in 50! x 20!?
questions.explanation: Zeroes in 50! = 12. Zeroes in 20! = 4. Product adds zeroes: 12 + 4 = 16.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes does the product 10 x 20 x 30 x ... x 1000 have?
questions.explanation: $10^{100}$ * 100!. 100! contributes 24 zeroes. 100 + 24 = 124 trailing zeroes.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the number of zeroes at the end of the sum (100! + 200!)?
questions.child_logic: Addition Bottleneck: When adding numbers, the smaller number dictates the trailing zeroes! 100! has 24 zeroes, 200! has 49 zeroes. Sum ends in 24 zeroes!
questions.explanation: When adding, e.g. 1000 + 100000 = 101000 (3 zeroes). The count is min(24, 49) = 24.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many zeroes are there at the end of 500!?

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many zeroes are there at the end of 1000!?

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many natural numbers n exist such that n! ends in exactly 24 zeroes?
questions.child_logic: Factorial jumps in steps of 5! 99! has 22 zeroes, 100! has 24 zeroes. The numbers 100, 101, 102, 103, 104 all end in 24 zeroes (5 numbers!). 105! jumps to 25.
questions.explanation: n = 100, 101, 102, 103, 104 all have 24 trailing zeroes. Exactly 5 values.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many natural numbers n exist such that n! ends in exactly 29 zeroes?
questions.child_logic: Jump Over: 124! has 28 zeroes. 125! has 125/5+125/25+125/125 = 25+5+1 = 31 zeroes! It jumps from 28 straight to 31. NO number ends in 29 or 30 zeroes!
questions.explanation: 124! has 28 zeroes. 125! adds three 5s, jumping to 31 zeroes. Hence, 0 natural numbers exist.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: Find the number of zeroes at the end of: $2^{2} \times 5^{4}$ x $4^{6} \times 10^{8}$ x $25^{10} \times 50^{12}$.
questions.explanation: Power of 2 is the bottleneck: 2 + 12 + 8 + 12 = 34. Power of 5 = 4 + 8 + 20 + 24 = 56. Trailing zeroes = 34.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the highest power of 3 that completely divides 100!?
questions.explanation: 33 + 11 + 3 + 1 = 48. Highest power of 3 is $3^{48}$.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the highest power of 7 that divides 100!?

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the highest power of 12 that divides 50!?
questions.explanation: Power of 3 is 22. Power of 4 is 23. The bottleneck is 3, so power of 12 is 22.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes are there in the product P = $1^{1} \times 2^{2}$ x $3^{3} \times 4^{4}$ x ... x $10^{10}$?
questions.child_logic: Only multiples of 5 contribute 5s: $5^{5}$ gives five 5s, and $10^{10}$ gives ten 5s. Total 5s = 5 + 10 = 15. 2s are abundant, so 15 zeroes!
questions.explanation: $5^{5}$ contributes 5, $10^{10}$ contributes 10. Total zeroes = 5 + 10 = 15.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many zeroes are at the end of (100! x 200!)?
questions.child_logic: Multiplication adds zeroes: 100! has 24 zeroes, 200! has [200/5]+[200/25]+[200/125] = 40+8+1 = 49 zeroes. Total = 24 + 49 = 73 zeroes!

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: Find the number of zeroes at the end of 80!.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes are there in 250!?

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the number of trailing zeroes in 120!?

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many zeroes are there at the end of the product of all even numbers from 2 to 100?
questions.explanation: $2^{50}$ * 50!. 50! has [50/5]+[50/25] = 12 zeroes. Power of 2 is massive, so 12 zeroes.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the number of trailing zeroes in (25!)^5?
questions.child_logic: 25! has [25/5] + [25/25] = 5 + 1 = 6 zeroes. Raised to power 5: 6 x 5 = 30 zeroes!
questions.explanation: Zeroes in 25! = 6. (25!)^5 has 6 * 5 = 30 zeroes.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes are there in 60! / 30!?
questions.child_logic: Division subtracts zeroes: 60! has [60/5]+[60/25] = 12+2 = 14 zeroes. 30! has [30/5]+[30/25] = 6+1 = 7 zeroes. 14 - 7 = 7 zeroes!

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: What is the rightmost non-zero digit of 30!?
questions.child_logic: Strip zeroes (remove all pairs of 2 and 5) and compute remaining product mod 10: gives 8!
questions.explanation: By modular arithmetic on non-5 and non-2 parts, the rightmost non-zero digit is 8.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes are in 45! + 46! + 47!?
questions.explanation: 45!(1 + 46 + 46*47) = 45! * 2209. 2209 is not divisible by 5, so zeroes = zeroes in 45! = 10.

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many trailing zeroes are there in 150!?

questions.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials & Products
questions.q: How many zeroes are there at the end of the product (5 x 15 x 25 x 35 x 45 x 55 x 65 x 75 x 85 x 95 x 128)?
questions.child_logic: 128 = $2^{7}$. Since there are only seven 2s in the entire product and plenty of 5s, the bottleneck is $2^{7}$ -> exactly 7 zeroes!
questions.explanation: 128 = $2^{7}$. All other numbers are odd multiples of 5. Power of 2 is 7. Trailing zeroes = 7.

csat-06.title: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
csat-06.mental_model: The ₹100 Bill: Anchor the unknown base to 100. If A is 25% more than B, B is 100, A is 125. Reciprocal shifts: +1/4 requires -1/5 to restore!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: If A's income is 25% more than B's income, by what percentage is B's income less than A's income?
questions.child_logic: Reciprocal Shift: An increase of +1/4 (25%) requires a drop of -1/5 (20%) on the higher base to return to the original!
questions.explanation: Let B = 100. Then A = 125. B is 25 less than A. Percentage less = (25 / 125) * 100 = 20%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: The price of cooking oil increases by 20%. By what percentage must a household reduce its consumption so that total expenditure remains unchanged?
questions.child_logic: Constant Product: Price rises by 1/5 (+20%). Quantity must fall by 1/(5+1) = 1/6 = 16.67%!
questions.explanation: Expenditure = Price * Quantity. Let original P=10, Q=10, E=100. New P=12. New Q = 100/12 = 8.33. Reduction = 10 - 8.33 = 1.67. % reduction = (1.67/10)*100 = 16.67%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: In an election between two candidates, the winning candidate secured 58% of the valid votes and won by a margin of 960 votes. Assuming all votes cast were valid, what was the total number of votes polled?
questions.child_logic: Tug-of-War: Winner gets 58%, so loser gets 42%. Margin = 58% - 42% = 16%. If 16% = 960, then 1% = 60, and 100% = 6,000!
questions.explanation: Winner = 58%, Loser = 100% - 58% = 42%. Difference = 16%. 16% of Total = 960. Total = 960 / 0.16 = 6,000.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: A candidate scored 32% marks in an examination and failed by 16 marks. Another candidate scored 44% marks and obtained 32 marks more than the minimum passing marks. What are the maximum marks of the examination?
questions.child_logic: Gap Jump: The percentage jump from 32% to 44% is 12%. The marks gap from -16 to +32 is 48 marks. 12% = 48 marks, so 100% = 400 marks!
questions.explanation: Difference in % = 44% - 32% = 12%. Difference in marks = 32 - (-16) = 48 marks. Total Marks = (48 / 12) * 100 = 400.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: A civil servant spends 75% of her monthly salary. When her salary is increased by 20%, she increases her monthly expenditure by 10%. By what percentage do her monthly savings increase?
questions.child_logic: Budget Box: Salary = 100, Spend = 75, Save = 25. New Salary = 120, New Spend = 75 + 7.5 = 82.5. New Save = 120 - 82.5 = 37.5. Jump from 25 to 37.5 is +50%!
questions.explanation:
Original: Income = 100, Exp = 75, Savings = 25.
New: Income = 120, Exp = 75 * 1.10 = 82.5, Savings = 120 - 82.5 = 37.5.
Increase in savings = (37.5 - 25) / 25 * 100 = 12.5 / 25 * 100 = 50%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: Fresh watermelons contain 96% water by weight. After being kept in the sun for 3 days, some water evaporates, leaving 80% water by weight. How many kg of dried watermelon will be obtained from 100 kg of fresh watermelon?
questions.child_logic: Pulp Lock: The solid pulp never evaporates! Fresh pulp = 4% of 100 kg = 4 kg. In dried fruit, water is 80%, so pulp is 20%. 20% of dried weight = 4 kg -> Dried weight = 20 kg!
questions.explanation:
Pulp content is constant.
Pulp in fresh fruit = (100 - 96)% of 100 kg = 4 kg.
Let dry fruit weight = W. In dry fruit, pulp is (100 - 80)% = 20%.
20% of W = 4 kg => W = 4 / 0.20 = 20 kg.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: After deducting a commission of 12.5% on gross sales, an agent remits ₹14,000 to the agricultural cooperative. What was the gross sales value?
questions.child_logic: Fraction Ladder: 12.5% = 1/8. Remitted amount = 7/8 of gross. 7 units = ₹14,000, so 1 unit = ₹2,000, and full 8 units = ₹16,000!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: In a rural district, 55% of the population are females. 40% of the females and 60% of the males are literate. What is the overall literacy rate of the district?
questions.child_logic: Weighted Sum: Take 100 citizens. Females = 55 (40% literate = 22). Males = 45 (60% literate = 27). Total literates = 22 + 27 = 49!
questions.explanation:
Let total population = 100. Females = 55, Males = 45.
Literate females = 55 * 0.40 = 22.
Literate males = 45 * 0.60 = 27.
Total literates = 22 + 27 = 49. Overall rate = 49%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: A reduction of 20% in the price of sugar enables a consumer to buy 4 kg more sugar for ₹960. What was the original price of sugar per kg?
questions.child_logic: Saved Money: 20% of ₹960 = ₹192 saved. This ₹192 buys 4 kg now, so reduced price = 192 / 4 = ₹48/kg. Since price was cut by 20% (4/5), original = 48 / 0.8 = ₹60/kg!
questions.explanation:
Amount saved = 20% of 960 = ₹192. Reduced price = 192 / 4 = ₹48 per kg.
Original price = 48 / (1 - 0.20) = 48 / 0.8 = ₹60 per kg.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: A student multiplied a positive number by 3/5 instead of multiplying it by 5/3. What is the percentage error in the calculated result?
questions.child_logic: LCM Base Anchor: Choose number = 15. Correct = 15 * (5/3) = 25. Wrong = 15 * (3/5) = 9. Shortfall = 25 - 9 = 16. Error % = (16 / 25) * 100 = 64%!
questions.explanation: Let number = 15. Correct result = 15 * 5/3 = 25. Incorrect result = 15 * 3/5 = 9. Error = 25 - 9 = 16. % Error = (16 / 25) * 100 = 64%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: In a competitive examination, 70% of candidates passed in English, 80% passed in Mathematics, and 10% failed in both subjects. If 144 candidates passed in both subjects, what was the total number of candidates who appeared?
questions.child_logic: Venn Overlap: Failed in both = 10%, so passed in at least one = 90%. Overlap = 70% + 80% - 90% = 60%. 60% = 144 students -> 100% = 240 students!
questions.explanation:
Total passed in at least one = 100% - 10% = 90%.
P(E U M) = P(E) + P(M) - P(E ∩ M) => 90% = 70% + 80% - P(Both) => P(Both) = 60%.
60% of Total = 144 => Total = 144 / 0.60 = 240.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: In manufacturing an engineering component, material costs account for 60% of total cost, labour accounts for 30%, and overhead accounts for 10%. If raw material prices rise by 20% and labour costs rise by 10%, what is the percentage increase in total manufacturing cost?
questions.child_logic: Cost Component Stack: Original Total = 100 (Material 60, Labour 30, Overhead 10). Material jump = 60 * 20% = 12. Labour jump = 30 * 10% = 3. Overhead = 0. Total jump = 12 + 3 = 15%!
questions.explanation:
Increase in material = 60 * 0.20 = 12.
Increase in labour = 30 * 0.10 = 3.
Total increase = 12 + 3 = 15 out of 100 = 15%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: If 20% of a number is added to 40, the result is the number itself. What is the number?
questions.child_logic: Complement Gap: If 20% + 40 = 100%, then 40 must equal the remaining 80%! 80% = 40, so 100% = 50!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: How much pure water must be added to 60 litres of an 80% sulfuric acid solution to dilute it to a 50% acid solution?
questions.child_logic: Acid Locked: Acid volume = 80% of 60 = 48 litres. In the final solution, these 48 litres must represent 50% of total! Total volume = 48 / 0.5 = 96 litres. Water added = 96 - 60 = 36 litres!
questions.explanation:
Acid amount = 60 * 0.80 = 48 litres.
In new solution, 48 litres = 50% of Total V.
Total V = 48 / 0.50 = 96 litres. Water added = 96 - 60 = 36 litres.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: Two numbers are respectively 20% and 50% more than a third number. What is the ratio of the first number to the second number?
questions.child_logic: Common Base: Let third number = 100. First = 120, Second = 150. Ratio = 120 / 150 = 4 / 5!
questions.explanation: Let third = 100. First = 120, Second = 150. Ratio = 120 : 150 = 4 : 5.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: In an election, 8% of voters on the electoral roll did not cast their votes. A candidate secured 48% of the total voters on the roll and defeated the only rival by 1,100 votes. What was the total number of voters registered on the roll?
questions.child_logic: Roll Breakdown: Total on roll = 100%. Did not vote = 8%. Total cast = 92%. Winner = 48%. Rival = 92% - 48% = 44%. Margin = 48% - 44% = 4%. If 4% = 1,100, then 100% = 27,500!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: A batsman scored 120 runs which included 4 boundaries and 6 sixes. What percentage of his total score did he make by running between the wickets?
questions.child_logic: Boundary Subtraction: 4 boundaries = 16 runs; 6 sixes = 36 runs. Total boundaries = 52 runs. Runs ran = 120 - 52 = 68 runs. Percentage = (68 / 120) * 100 = 56.67%!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 20% and its denominator is decreased by 10%, the resulting fraction becomes 16/21. What was the original fraction?

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: In an office, 40% of the staff are female. 70% of female staff and 50% of male staff are married. What percentage of the total staff in the office are unmarried?
questions.child_logic: Unmarried Hunt: Out of 100: Female = 40 (30% unmarried = 12). Male = 60 (50% unmarried = 30). Total unmarried = 12 + 30 = 42%!
questions.explanation:
Staff = 100. Female = 40, Male = 60.
Unmarried female = 40 * (1 - 0.70) = 12.
Unmarried male = 60 * (1 - 0.50) = 30.
Total unmarried = 12 + 30 = 42.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: The income tax rate is reduced from 25% to 20%, but due to inflation, a professional's taxable income increases by 20%. What is the net percentage change in the tax paid by the professional?
questions.child_logic: Tax Bill: Old = 100 income * 25% = 25 tax. New = 120 income * 20% = 24 tax. Tax fell from 25 to 24: (1 / 25) * 100 = 4% decrease!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: A number is first increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. What is the net percentage change in the number?
questions.child_logic: Symmetric Fall: 100 -> 110 -> 110 - 11 = 99. A net drop of 1%!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: In a municipal survey of 1,000 residents, 60% read Hindi newspapers, 50% read English newspapers, and 20% read neither. How many residents read both Hindi and English newspapers?
questions.child_logic: Union Complement: Neither = 20%, so at least one = 80% = 800 people. Both = 600 + 500 - 800 = 300 people!
questions.explanation:
Total reading at least one = 1,000 * 0.80 = 800.
n(H ∩ E) = n(H) + n(E) - n(H U E) = 600 + 500 - 800 = 300.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: If x is 80% of y, what percentage of 2x is y?
questions.child_logic: Value Substitution: Let y = 100. Then x = 80. 2x = 160. Percentage of 2x that y represents = (100 / 160) * 100 = 62.5%!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: A public library has 40% Hindi literature books, 25% of the remaining are English history books, and the remaining 36,000 books are in regional languages. What is the total collection of books in the library?
questions.child_logic: Chain of Remnants: Remaining after Hindi = 60%. History is 25% of that, so regional is 75% of 60% = 45% of total! If 45% = 36,000, then 100% = 80,000!

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: If the price of petrol increases by 25%, by how much should a motorist reduce travel distance so that fuel expenditure increases by only 10%?
questions.child_logic: Ratio Adjustment: Expenditure = P * Q. 1.10 = 1.25 * Q => Q = 1.10 / 1.25 = 0.88. Distance must drop by 1 - 0.88 = 12%!
questions.explanation:
New Exp = 1.10, New Price = 1.25.
New Quantity = 1.10 / 1.25 = 0.88.
Reduction in quantity = (1 - 0.88) * 100 = 12%.

questions.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction-Percentage Ladder
questions.q: The central government allocation for a highway project was ₹4,800 Crore in Phase 1 and was increased to ₹6,480 Crore in Phase 2. What is the percentage increase in the allocation?
questions.child_logic: Allocation Jump: Difference = 6,480 - 4,800 = ₹1,680 Crore. Percentage = (1,680 / 4,800) * 100 = 35%!
questions.explanation:
Increase = 6480 - 4800 = 1680.
Percentage increase = (1680 / 4800) * 100 = 35%.

csat-07.title: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
csat-07.mental_model: Net Effect Machine: Net % = a + b + (ab/100). Equal increase and decrease always produces a loss of (x/10)^2 percent!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A town's population increases by 10% in the first year and by 20% in the second year. What is the net percentage increase in population over the two years?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The length of a rectangular plot is increased by 30% and its breadth is decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change in the area of the plot?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The radius of a circular helipad is increased by 50%. What is the percentage increase in its surface area?
questions.child_logic: Circle Area Scales as $r^{2}$: (1.5)^2 = 2.25. The area jumps from 1.0 to 2.25, which is a 125% increase!
questions.explanation: Area = pi * $r^{2}$. If r becomes 1.5r, area becomes 2.25 * Area. Increase = (2.25 - 1) * 100 = 125%.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The value of a heavy excavation machine depreciates by 10% every year. If its present value is ₹8,10,000, what was its value 2 years ago?
questions.child_logic: Reverse Depreciation: Each year it retains 90% (9/10). After 2 years it retains (9/10)^2 = 81/100. If 81 units = ₹8,10,000, 100 units = ₹10,00,000!
questions.explanation:
Present Value = Original * (1 - 0.10)^2 = Original * 0.81.
Original = 810000 / 0.81 = ₹10,00,000.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: In a cylindrical water storage tank, the radius of the base is increased by 20% while its height is reduced by 50%. What is the percentage change in the volume of the tank?
questions.child_logic: Cylinder Volume = pi * $r^{2}$ * h: Radius squared = (1.2)^2 = 1.44. Height = 0.5. Net factor = 1.44 * 0.5 = 0.72. The volume drops from 1.0 to 0.72, a 28% decrease!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A cinema hall reduces its ticket price by 20%, resulting in a 40% increase in daily visitor attendance. What is the net percentage change in daily revenue collection?
questions.child_logic: Price x Quantity: Net % = -20 + 40 + (-20 * 40)/100 = 20 - 8 = +12% increase!
questions.explanation: Revenue = Price * Attendance. Net change = -20 + 40 - (20*40)/100 = 20 - 8 = +12%.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The side of a square foundation is increased by 20%. By what percentage does its perimeter increase, and by what percentage does its area increase?
questions.child_logic: Linear vs Quadratic: Perimeter is 4s (linear), so it increases by exactly 20%. Area is $s^{2}$, so net change is 20 + 20 + 4 = 44%!
questions.explanation:
Perimeter P = 4s. Increase = 20%.
Area A = $s^{2}$. Increase = 20 + 20 + (20*20)/100 = 44%.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: Successive discounts of 10%, 20%, and 25% on an electronic tablet are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.child_logic: Multiplier Cascade: ₹100 -> 90 -> 90 - 18 = 72 -> 72 - 18 = ₹54 remaining. Total discount = 100 - 54 = 46%!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The radius of a sphere is reduced by 10%. By what percentage does its volume decrease?
questions.child_logic: Sphere Volume $r^{3}$: (0.9)^3 = 0.729. Net volume remaining is 72.9%. Drop = 100 - 72.9 = 27.1%!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: An employee's salary was first increased by 20% and later decreased by 20%. What is the net change in his salary?
questions.child_logic: Square Rule: (x/10)^2 = (20/10)^2 = 4% loss!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The population of a city was 1,20,000. It increased by 10% in the first year, increased by 20% in the second year, and then decreased by 15% in the third year due to an epidemic. What was the population at the end of the third year?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The dimensions of a rectangular godown are altered: length is increased by 10%, breadth is decreased by 10%, and height is increased by 20%. What is the net percentage change in the godown's volume?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: An article listed at ₹1,000 is sold for ₹720 after two successive discounts. If the first discount is 10%, what is the percentage of the second discount?
questions.child_logic: Intermediate Price: ₹1,000 after 10% discount becomes ₹900. Price drops from ₹900 to ₹720, a discount of ₹180. (180 / 900) * 100 = 20%!
questions.explanation:
Price after 1st discount = 1000 * 0.90 = ₹900.
Second discount amount = 900 - 720 = ₹180.
Second discount % = (180 / 900) * 100 = 20%.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: If the tax on a commodity is increased by 15% and its consumption decreases by 10%, what is the percentage change in the total revenue collected from the commodity?
questions.explanation: Revenue = Tax * Consumption. Net change = 15 - 10 - (15*10)/100 = 5 - 1.5 = +3.5% (increase).

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A merchant raises the price of an article by 40% and then allows a discount of 25% on the increased price. What is his net gain percentage?
questions.child_logic: 100 Anchor: ₹100 marked to ₹140. 25% discount on ₹140 = ₹35 off. Selling price = 140 - 35 = ₹105. Net profit = 5%!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: In a laboratory culture, bacterial population increases by 10% in the first hour, 20% in the second hour, and 25% in the third hour. If the initial count was 10,000, what is the count after 3 hours?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A government employee's salary was reduced by 25%. By what percentage must his reduced salary be raised to restore it to its original amount?
questions.child_logic: Restoration Jump: Salary fell from 100 to 75 (a drop of 25). To go from 75 back to 100, we must add 25 on base 75: (25/75)*100 = 33.33%!
questions.explanation: Reduced salary = 75. Required increase = 25. % increase = (25 / 75) * 100 = 33.33%.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: Due to drought, the water level in an irrigation reservoir dropped by 20% in May and by another 25% of the remaining level in June. What is the total percentage reduction in water level over the two months?
questions.child_logic: Water Remaining: May leaves 80%. June leaves 75% of 80% = 60%. Total drop = 100 - 60 = 40%!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The radius of the base of a right circular cone is increased by 10% while its slant height remains unchanged. What is the percentage increase in its curved surface area?
questions.child_logic: Linear r in Area: Curved Surface Area = pi * r * l. Since l is constant, CSA is directly proportional to r! 10% increase in r gives exactly 10% increase in CSA!
questions.explanation: CSA = pi * r * l. Since l is unchanged, CSA' = pi * (1.10r) * l = 1.10 * CSA. Increase = 10%.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A property dealer buys land whose value appreciates by 15% every year. If its value after 2 years is ₹52,900, what was its original purchase price?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: The cost of production of a smartphone consists of 50% components, 30% assembly, and 20% logistics. Component prices surge by 30%, assembly costs drop by 10%, and logistics costs rise by 15%. What is the net percentage change in total production cost?
questions.child_logic: Weighted Sum: Component jump = 50 * 0.30 = +15. Assembly jump = 30 * -0.10 = -3. Logistics jump = 20 * 0.15 = +3. Net jump = +15 - 3 + 3 = +15%!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A trader offers two successive discounts of 15% and 10% on an item. What is the overall percentage discount?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A cubical wooden block has its length increased by 10%, breadth decreased by 20%, and height increased by 30%. What is the percentage change in the volume of the block?
questions.child_logic: Volume Factor: 1.10 * 0.80 * 1.30 = 0.88 * 1.30 = 1.144. Volume increases by 14.4%!
questions.explanation: New Volume = 1.10 * 0.80 * 1.30 * V = 1.144 V. Net volume increase = 14.4%.

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A state's forest cover declined by 5% per decade for two consecutive decades. What is the cumulative percentage loss in forest cover over the 20-year period?

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A merchant marks up his goods by 50% above cost price and then gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is his overall profit percentage?
questions.child_logic: Trace ₹100: Cost = 100. Marked = 150. After 20% off = 150 - 30 = 120. After 10% off = 120 - 12 = 108. Profit = 8%!

questions.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes, Population & Compounding
questions.q: A public transport authority increased bus fares by 25%. Consequently, passenger traffic declined by 16%. What was the net percentage change in total daily revenue?
questions.child_logic: Revenue = Fare * Traffic: 1.25 * 0.84 = 1.05. A 5% increase!

csat-08.title: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
csat-08.mental_model: Vendor Scale & Markup: False weight profit % = [Error / (True Weight - Error)] * 100. Selling two items at same SP with equal gain/loss % always incurs a net loss of (x/10)^2 percent!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A trader sells an article for ₹840 and thereby incurs a loss of 20%. At what price should he sell it to gain 20%?

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: If the cost price of 16 articles is equal to the selling price of 12 articles, what is the profit percentage?
questions.child_logic: Article Equivalence: 16 CP = 12 SP => SP/CP = 16/12 = 4/3. Profit is 1 on CP 3: (1/3)*100 = 33.33%!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A merchant sells two handlooms for ₹9,900 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall gain or loss percentage on the entire transaction?
questions.child_logic: Twin SP Theorem: When two goods are sold at the same SP with equal profit and loss %, there is ALWAYS a net loss of (x/10)^2 = (10/10)^2 = 1%!
questions.explanation: Twin SP formula: Loss % = (Common % / 10)^2 = (10/10)^2 = 1% loss.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A dishonest ration dealer professes to sell wheat at cost price, but uses a false weight of 900 grams for a 1-kg measure. What is his actual profit percentage?
questions.child_logic: Faulty Scale Ratio: Error = 100g. What he actually gives away = 900g. Profit = (Error / True - Error) * 100 = (100 / 900) * 100 = 11.11%!
questions.explanation: Gain % = [Error / (True Weight - Error)] * 100 = (100 / 900) * 100 = 11.11%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 20% above the cost price and then offers a discount of 10% on the marked price. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.child_logic: Anchor ₹100: CP = 100. MP = 120. Discount 10% of 120 = 12. SP = 120 - 12 = 108. Profit = 8%!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: Under a promotional scheme 'Buy 3, Get 1 Free', what is the effective percentage discount offered to the customer?
questions.child_logic: Cart Proportion: Customer gets 4 items in total, but pays for only 3. 1 item out of 4 is free: (1/4)*100 = 25% discount!
questions.explanation: Effective Discount % = [Free Articles / Total Articles] * 100 = (1 / 4) * 100 = 25%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: Under a promotional scheme 'Buy 4, Get 1 Free', what is the effective percentage discount?
questions.child_logic: Cart Proportion: Total items = 5. Free items = 1. Discount = (1/5)*100 = 20%!
questions.explanation: Effective Discount % = (1 / 5) * 100 = 20%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A dishonest merchant marks up his goods by 20% above cost price and also uses a false scale of 800 grams instead of 1,000 grams. What is his overall profit percentage?
questions.child_logic: Two-Way Cheat: Markup gives 1.20. False weight gives 1000/800 = 1.25. Total multiplier = 1.20 * 1.25 = 1.50 -> 50% profit!
questions.explanation: Effective multiplier = (1.20) * (1000 / 800) = 1.20 * 1.25 = 1.50. Total profit = 50%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: The cost price of an article is ₹640. If the seller wishes to make a profit of 20% after allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price, what should be the marked price?

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A fruit vendor buys 100 dozen bananas at ₹40 per dozen. During transit, 10 dozen bananas get damaged and cannot be sold. At what price per dozen should he sell the remaining bananas to make an overall profit of 20%?
questions.child_logic: Salvage Math: Total cost = 100 * 40 = ₹4,000. Desired revenue = 4,000 * 1.20 = ₹4,800. Bananas left = 90 dozen. Price per dozen = 4,800 / 90 = ₹53.33!
questions.explanation:
Total CP = 100 * 40 = ₹4,000. Desired SP = 4000 * 1.20 = ₹4,800.
Sellable dozens = 90. SP per dozen = 4800 / 90 = ₹53.33.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: By selling an article for ₹720, a shopkeeper gains 20%. What would have been the gain or loss percentage if he had sold it for ₹540?

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: The profit earned by selling an article for ₹832 is equal to the loss incurred when the same article is sold for ₹448. What should be the selling price of the article to make a profit of 50%?
questions.child_logic: Midpoint CP: CP is exactly halfway between profit SP and loss SP: CP = (832 + 448) / 2 = 1280 / 2 = ₹640. To make 50% profit: 640 * 1.5 = ₹960!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A wholesaler sells a water purifier to a distributor at 10% profit. The distributor sells it to a retailer at 20% profit, and the retailer sells it to a customer for ₹7,920 at 20% profit. What was the production cost of the purifier for the wholesaler?

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: If the selling price of an article is increased from an 8% profit to a 15% profit, the seller realizes ₹140 more. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.child_logic: Profit Gap: Jump from 8% to 15% is 7%. If 7% of CP = ₹140, then 1% = ₹20, and 100% CP = ₹2,000!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A cloth merchant professes to sell cloth at cost price, but uses a measuring meter rod that is actually only 95 cm long. What is his profit percentage?
questions.child_logic: Scale Ratio: Gives 95 cm instead of 100 cm. Profit = (5 / 95) * 100 = 100 / 19 = 5.26%!
questions.explanation: Profit % = [Error / Given Measure] * 100 = (5 / 95) * 100 = 5.26%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A publisher sells 2/3 of an edition of books at a profit of 15% and the remaining 1/3 at a loss of 6%. What is his overall profit percentage on the entire edition?
questions.child_logic: Weighted Sum: (2/3 * 15%) + (1/3 * -6%) = 10% - 2% = 8% overall profit!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A person buys an old bicycle for ₹1,500 and spends ₹300 on its repair and painting. He then sells it for ₹2,250. What is his profit percentage?

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: By selling an article at 2/3 of the marked price, there is a loss of 10%. What is the profit percentage if the article is sold at the marked price?
questions.child_logic: Fraction Anchor: At 2/3 MP, SP = 90% CP. So (2/3) MP = 0.90 CP => MP = 0.90 * (3/2) CP = 1.35 CP. Selling at MP yields 35% profit!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A trader buys 50 kg of pulses at ₹60 per kg. He sells 30 kg at 10% profit. At what profit percentage must he sell the remaining 20 kg to achieve an overall profit of 20% on the entire stock?
questions.child_logic: Deviation Seesaw: 30 kg is +10% below target of 20% (deficit = 30 * -10 = -300). Remaining 20 kg must make up +300: 300 / 20 = +15% above target = 20% + 15% = 35%!
questions.explanation:
Total profit required = 50 * 20 = 1,000 units.
Profit from first 30 kg = 30 * 10 = 300 units.
Profit needed from remaining 20 kg = 1,000 - 300 = 700 units.
Required % = 700 / 20 = 35%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A merchant allows a discount of 10% on the marked price of a solar panel. How much above the cost price must he mark it so as to gain 17% on the cost price?
questions.child_logic: Markup Formula: (MP - CP) / CP: MP * 0.90 = 1.17 CP => MP = 1.17 / 0.90 CP = 1.30 CP. Markup is 30%!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: If an article is sold at 80% of its regular selling price, there is a loss of 12%. What is the profit percentage at the regular selling price?
questions.child_logic: Scale Ratio: 0.80 SP = 0.88 CP => SP = 0.88 / 0.80 CP = 1.10 CP. Regular SP gives 10% profit!
questions.explanation: 0.80 SP = 0.88 CP => SP = 1.10 CP. Profit at regular SP = 10%.

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A retailer buys 20 items for ₹1,000. He marks them up by 40%. He sells 12 items at this marked price, 5 items at a 10% discount on marked price, and the remaining 3 items at cost price. What is his total net profit?
questions.child_logic: Sum Receipts: Cost per item = ₹50. Marked = ₹70. 12 items @ ₹70 = ₹840. 5 items @ ₹63 = ₹315. 3 items @ ₹50 = ₹150. Total revenue = 840 + 315 + 150 = ₹1,305. Net profit = 1,305 - 1,000 = ₹305!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A dealer purchased a tractor for ₹4,00,000 and spent ₹20,000 on registration and insurance. If he sells it for ₹4,62,000, what is his profit percentage?

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A seller incurs a 5% loss by selling a book for ₹190. If he sells it for ₹220, what is his gain or loss percentage?

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: An unprincipled vendor cheats by 10% in weight while buying raw grains and also cheats by 10% in weight while selling to customers. Assuming he sells at cost price, what is his total profit percentage?
questions.child_logic: Weight Multiplication: Takes 1100g for 1000g cost. Sells 900g for 1000g revenue. Ratio = 1100 / 900 = 11 / 9. Profit = 2 / 9 = 22.22%!

questions.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
questions.q: A dairy cooperative procures milk at ₹45 per litre. It adds water to the milk and sells the diluted mixture at ₹50 per litre, thereby making a profit of 25%. What is the ratio of water to milk in the mixture?
questions.child_logic: Alligation / Unit Math: To make 25% profit at ₹50, cost of mixture must be 50 / 1.25 = ₹40/litre. Alligation of Milk (₹45) and Water (₹0) with Mean (₹40): Water/Milk = (45 - 40) / (40 - 0) = 5 / 40 = 1 : 8!
questions.explanation:
Effective CP of mixture = 50 / 1.25 = ₹40 per litre.
By alligation: Milk (45) vs Water (0), Mean = 40.
Ratio Milk : Water = (40 - 0) : (45 - 40) = 40 : 5 = 8 : 1.
Ratio Water : Milk = 1 : 8.

csat-09.title: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
csat-09.mental_model: Seesaw Balancing Scale: Sum of positive deviations equals sum of negative deviations from the fulcrum average. Replacement weight = Old Weight + (N * Change in Average)!

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: The average weight of a group of 8 officers increases by 2.5 kg when an officer weighing 65 kg is replaced by a new recruit. What is the weight of the new recruit?
questions.child_logic: Seesaw Push: The new recruit must carry the old 65 kg PLUS boost all 8 members by 2.5 kg: 65 + (8 * 2.5) = 65 + 20 = 85 kg!
questions.explanation: Weight of new person = Replaced weight + (Number of people * Increase in avg) = 65 + (8 * 2.5) = 65 + 20 = 85 kg.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: The average age of 24 students in a classroom is 14 years. If the teacher's age is included, the average age increases by 1 year. What is the teacher's age?
questions.child_logic: Group Expansion: There are now 25 people with average 15. Teacher = 15 + (24 * 1) = 39 years!
questions.explanation: Teacher's age = New average + (Previous count * Increase) = 15 + (24 * 1) = 39 years.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: A batsman has a certain average of runs for 16 innings. In the 17th innings, he scores 85 runs and thereby increases his average by 3 runs. What is his new batting average after the 17th innings?
questions.child_logic: Run Allocation: The 85 runs gave 3 runs to each of the 16 previous innings (16 * 3 = 48 runs). His new average is the remainder: 85 - 48 = 37 runs!
questions.explanation:
Let old average = A. New average = A + 3.
16A + 85 = 17(A + 3) => 16A + 85 = 17A + 51 => A = 34.
New average = 34 + 3 = 37.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: A cricket bowler's bowling average was 12.4 runs per wicket. In his next match, he takes 5 wickets for 26 runs, thereby improving his bowling average by 0.4 runs. How many total wickets had he taken prior to this match?
questions.child_logic: Alligation on Bowling Avg: Old avg = 12.4, Match avg = 26/5 = 5.2. New overall avg = 12.4 - 0.4 = 12.0. Cross ratio: (12.0 - 5.2) / (12.4 - 12.0) = 6.8 / 0.4 = 17 : 1. If 1 unit = 5 wickets, 17 units = 85 wickets!
questions.explanation:
Match bowling average = 26 / 5 = 5.2.
By alligation: (12.4 - 12.0) = 0.4 vs (12.0 - 5.2) = 6.8.
Ratio of wickets = 6.8 : 0.4 = 17 : 1.
Previous wickets = 17 * 5 = 85 wickets.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: The average score of 50 students in an examination was calculated as 68. Later, it was discovered that the score of one student was mistakenly recorded as 88 instead of the correct score of 38. What is the correct average score?
questions.child_logic: Excess Subtraction: Excess marks recorded = 88 - 38 = 50 marks. Spread across 50 students, the average was inflated by 50/50 = 1 mark! Correct average = 68 - 1 = 67!
questions.explanation:
Correction = 38 - 88 = -50.
Change in average = -50 / 50 = -1.
Correct average = 68 - 1 = 67.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: The average temperature for Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday was 40°C. The average temperature for Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday was 41°C. If the temperature on Thursday was 42°C, what was the temperature on Monday?
questions.child_logic: Sliding Window: (Tue + Wed + Thu) - (Mon + Tue + Wed) = Thu - Mon = 3 * 41 - 3 * 40 = 3°C. If Thu = 42°C, Mon = 42 - 3 = 39°C!
questions.explanation: (Tue + Wed + Thu) - (Mon + Tue + Wed) = 3(41) - 3(40) = 3°C => Thu - Mon = 3°C => Mon = 42 - 3 = 39°C.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: A motorist travels from Town A to Town B at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns from Town B to Town A along the same route at 40 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip?
questions.explanation: Average speed for equal distances = 2 * S1 * S2 / (S1 + S2) = 2 * 60 * 40 / 100 = 48 km/h.

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: Nine friends went to a local dhaba for lunch. Eight of them spent ₹30 each on their meal, while the ninth person spent ₹20 more than the average expenditure of all nine people. What was the total amount spent by all nine friends?
questions.child_logic: Deviation Balance: The extra ₹20 spent by the 9th person covers the shortfall for the other 8 people! Shortfall per person = 20 / 8 = ₹2.50. Average = 30 + 2.50 = ₹32.50. Total = 9 * 32.50 = ₹292.50!

questions.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale & Cricket Innings
questions.q: What is the average of all prime numbers between 20 and 45?
